families.title: Pebble Duel: buckets
families.mathematics: Buckets stand in a row, each holding some fish. A move takes one fish from a bucket and may add one fish to each bucket to its left; whoever takes the last fish wins. Every play ends, because the rightmost bucket never gains a fish (and then, by induction, the buckets to its left), even though the number of fish can grow. The second player wins exactly when every bucket holds an even number: a move from such a position makes the bucket it takes from odd, and from any other position exactly one move restores it, taking from the rightmost odd bucket and adding one to each odd bucket on its left. The same holds with no limit on what is added. In the encore a move takes 1, 2 or 3 fish and may add up to 3 to each bucket on the left, and the second player wins exactly when every bucket is a multiple of 4; with adds of only 1 or 2 that fails.
rules: Players take turns. A move takes one fish from a bucket and may then add one fish to each bucket to its left, to some of them, or to none.
In the encore a move takes 1, 2 or 3 fish from one bucket and may add up to 3 fish to each bucket to its left.
Whoever takes the last fish wins. The app never misses a winning move.

puzzles.title: 0, 0 and 1
puzzles.objective: Take the last fish to win. You go first.
puzzles.instruction: Take the last fish to win. You go first.
puzzles.controls: A move takes one fish from a bucket and may add one fish to each bucket to its left. Whoever takes the last fish wins. Tap a bucket to take a fish from it, tap buckets to its left to add one to each, then End turn. Tap a bucket again to change it. I reply at once. Undo takes back your move and my reply.
rules: Players take turns.
A move takes one fish from a bucket.
It may then add one fish to each bucket to its left, to some of them, or to none.
Whoever takes the last fish wins.
The app never misses a winning move.
You go first.
puzzles.idea: Adding fish is allowed, never required. From 0, 0 and 1, take the fish and add nothing: then I have no move.
puzzles.prerequisites: Count to 3. A grown-up can read how a move works.
hints: After your move, what can I do?
If you leave me a fish, I can take it.
Take the fish from bucket 3, and add nothing.

parent.notice: Whether your child adds fish because the rule allows it, and changes course after I take a fish they gave me.
parent.prompt: Why did adding a fish lose?
parent.explanation: The only fish is in bucket 3, so the first move takes it and may add one fish to bucket 1, bucket 2, both or neither. Adding nothing leaves no fish, and the second player cannot move. Any addition leaves a bucket with one fish, which I take, and then you cannot move. Adding is a choice, and here the winning choice is none.
parent.connection: A normal-play impartial game: a start is lost for the player to move exactly when every move reaches a start that is won (Ferguson, §1). Hamkins’s buckets of fish show a game whose positions grow yet every play ends, by an ordinal ω^(n−1)·a_n + … + a_1 that drops at every move; parity in each bucket decides who wins.

puzzles.provenance: Week 81 Problem 1 (the start 0, 0 and 1: which starts let the first player win whatever the second player does?), as a duel against a perfect opponent.

puzzles.idea: The winning move takes from bucket 3 and adds to bucket 2 but not to bucket 1, leaving 2, 2 and 0.

parent.notice: Whether your child compares the buckets I leave after my moves, and tries leaving me something like them.
parent.prompt: Why does adding to bucket 1 as well lose?
parent.explanation: The second player wins exactly when every bucket holds an even number of fish. A move from such a position makes the bucket it takes from odd, so it always leaves an odd bucket. From any other position, take a fish from the rightmost odd bucket and add one to each odd bucket on its left (and none to the even ones): every bucket is even again, and this is the only move that does it. Every play ends (the rightmost bucket never gains a fish), so whoever keeps every bucket even takes the last fish. From 2, 1 and 1 the rightmost odd bucket is bucket 3, and bucket 2 is the only odd bucket on its left: take from 3 and add to 2, leaving 2, 2 and 0.

puzzles.title: Replies to 2 and 2

Tap a bucket to take a fish from it, tap buckets to its left to add one to each, then End turn. Tap a bucket again to change it. puzzles.idea: Going second from 2 and 2 wins against every first move: answer 1 and 2 with 0 and 2, answer 2 and 1 with 2 and 0, and answer 3 and 1 with 4 and 0.

parent.prompt: Why can I never win from 2 and 2 if I go first?
parent.explanation: The second player wins exactly when every bucket holds an even number of fish. A move from such a position makes the bucket it takes from odd, so it always leaves an odd bucket. puzzles.title: Two buckets of 0 to 3
puzzles.objective: Mark every start where you would rather go second, then press That’s all.
puzzles.visibleObjective: Mark every start where you would rather go second.
puzzles.instruction: Mark every start where you would rather go second, then press That’s all.
puzzles.controls: A move takes one fish from a bucket and may add one fish to each bucket to its left. Whoever takes the last fish wins. Tap a card to mark it, and again to clear it. Play, then a card, tries a game from it against me. That’s all checks every mark at once. While a start is still missing, it says “There is another.” Once none is missing, it is final: if a marked start is one where the first player can win, I go first from it and win, and then the marks are cleared.

parent.prompt: How do you know there is no other?
parent.explanation: The second player wins exactly when every bucket holds an even number of fish. A move from such a position makes the bucket it takes from odd, so it always leaves an odd bucket. From any other position, take a fish from the rightmost odd bucket and add one to each odd bucket on its left (and none to the even ones): every bucket is even again, and this is the only move that does it. Every play ends (the rightmost bucket never gains a fish), so whoever keeps every bucket even takes the last fish. So among the fifteen cards the second-player starts are 2 and 0, 0 and 2, and 2 and 2. While a start is missing, That’s all says only “There is another.”, with no count, even if a wrong card is marked too. Once none is missing, a wrong That’s all is final: the app goes first from the wrong card, wins, and clears the marks.

puzzles.title: Up to 3: 3 and 6
puzzles.objective: Take the last fish to win. You go first.
puzzles.visibleObjective: Take 1, 2 or 3 at a time, add up to 3 to each bucket on the left, and take the last fish.
puzzles.instruction: Take the last fish to win. You go first.
puzzles.controls: A move takes 1, 2 or 3 fish from one bucket and may add up to 3 fish to each bucket to its left. Whoever takes the last fish wins. Tap a bucket to take a fish from it, and again to take more, up to 3; tap a bucket to its left to add a fish, and again to add more, up to 3; one more tap puts them back. Then End turn. I reply at once. Undo takes back your move and my reply.
rules: Players take turns.
A move takes 1, 2 or 3 fish from one bucket.
It may then add up to 3 fish to each bucket to its left.
Whoever takes the last fish wins.
The app never misses a winning move.
You go first.
puzzles.idea: With takes of 1 to 3 and adds of up to 3, the starts to hand over are those where every bucket is a multiple of 4. From 3 and 6, take 2 from bucket 2 and add 1 to bucket 1, leaving 4 and 4.
hints: Try a move. When I win, Undo and look at what I left you.
When I won, how many fish did I leave in each bucket?
Take 2 from bucket 2 and add 1 to bucket 1, leaving 4 and 4.

parent.notice: Whether your child looks for a new kind of start to hand over, rather than keeping every bucket even.
parent.prompt: Why does 2 and 2 no longer win for the second player?
parent.explanation: With takes of 1, 2 or 3 and adds of up to 3, the second player wins exactly when every bucket is a multiple of 4. A move from such a position changes the bucket it takes from by 1 to 3, so it is no longer a multiple of 4. From any other position, take from the rightmost bucket that is not a multiple of 4 what is over the last multiple of 4, and add to each bucket on its left what it lacks of the next one (0 to 3): every bucket is a multiple of 4 again, and only that move does it. The adds of up to 3 matter: with adds of at most 1 or 2 the rule fails, already at 1 and 1. From 3 and 6, take 2 from bucket 2 (leaving 4) and add 1 to bucket 1 (making 4).
parent.extension: What if a move could take 1 to 4 and add up to 4?
parent.connection: A normal-play impartial game: a start is lost for the player to move exactly when every move reaches a start that is won (Ferguson, §1). Hamkins’s buckets of fish show a game whose positions grow yet every play ends, by an ordinal ω^(n−1)·a_n + … + a_1 that drops at every move; parity in each bucket decides who wins. The encore is the same argument with 4 in place of 2.

puzzles.provenance: Week 81 guide, encore (take 1, 2 or 3 and refill up to 3 to the left; multiples of four as the new losing target), as a duel; the start is new.
